_README: Labelled eval set for the agent tool router. 200 cases.
SPLIT DISCIPLINE. `split` is `dev` or `holdout`. The dev split (the original
26 cases plus additions) is what tuning was measured against. The holdout
split was written WITHOUT consulting scores and must not be used to tune --
it exists so an honest generalisation number is available. Report both; if
dev >> holdout, the constants are overfitted.
ANTI-LEAKAGE. `phrasing` records how the request was written relative to the
tool's own description:
vocabulary  - deliberately reuses the tool's description terms (easy case)
paraphrase  - describes the intent in words a user would pick, avoiding the
description's vocabulary (the case keyword matching fails)
oblique     - names the goal, not the operation ('who broke the build')
compound    - needs two or more tools
padded      - a real request wrapped in conversational filler
adversarial - contains vocabulary that pulls toward the WRONG tool
fail-open   - too short or too vague to route; must retain everything
`needed` lists tools a competent operator would call. Kept deliberately
small: a label the router cannot reasonably be expected to find is a bad
label, not a bad router. Every name is verified to exist in the live surface
by the harness, which errors out on a stale label.
ADVERSARIAL cases are the most valuable and the easiest to get wrong: the
`needed` tool must genuinely be the right answer despite the misleading
vocabulary, otherwise the case tests nothing.
